answer: The identity is a surveyed site with a sealed geophone. Each epoch the seed names one quake and a thirty-minute window; the agent files P and S arrivals plus peak amplitude, matched against the reference and the site's noise floor, which swells with the horizon glow at dawn, dropping inside a canyon. Stations within forty kilometres, or a shared owner, fold into one vote. Kit and survey run $4,900; a thousand clones cost $4.9 million in quiet ground, and a forged trace dies when its coda will not match. A seismograph is a stethoscope on one hillside; nobody lends you a heartbeat.
